paper.title: FORGE: Self-Evolving Agent Memory With No Weight Updates via Population Broadcast
paper.central_claim: FORGE couples same-model failure-triggered reflection with population champion broadcast and graduation to evolve persistent prompt memory, improving frozen post-session CAGE-2 B_line 30-step returns over zero-shot and isolated Reflexion across four model families and three representations; broadcast carries gains and graduation mainly saves compute.

evidence.quote:
. Yet most such agents remain single-episode systems: they reason and act within an episode, but retain little actionable knowledge that reliably improves future behavior. This gap is especially problematic in stochastic, partially observable environments where policies must be discovered through repeated interactions rather than specified in advance.

Since fine-tuning is often infeasible and expensive, prompt-only self-improvement offers a promising alternative. However, three critical questions remain for applying this to stochastic, long-horizon sequential decision-making: (1)
What should be remembered?
Existing approaches typically commit to a single representation (heuristics/rules or behavior examples) without controlled comparison. (2)
How should memory propagate?
Unlike serial reflection, population-based training suggests parallel exploration could accelerate learning, but its prompt-only analogue is underexplored. (3)
Is the training method transferable across LLMs?
Whether gradient-free evolution yields consistent gains across diverse model families remains an open empirical question.
evidence.support_explanation: Gap separates memory representation, population propagation and cross-family repeatability, rather than treating frozen weights as the contribution.

evidence.quote:
A growing body of literature explores replacing weight updates with linguistic feedback. Reflexion
(
Shinn et al., 2023
)
stores critiques after failures, while Self-Refine
(
Madaan et al., 2023
)
applies iterative critiques within a single response. CLIN
(
Majumder et al., 2024
)
extends prompt-only self-improvement to cross-episode causal-memory abstractions. Recent work on context evolution and test-time adaptation highlights that unconstrained self-edits can accumulate errors, motivating mechanisms that select and propagate only robust improvements across trials
(
Zhang et al., 2025
;
Suzgun et al., 2025
)
. TextGrad
(
Yuksekgonul et al., 2024
)
takes a complementary approach, performing gradient descent over text representations using LLM-generated feedback as the optimization signal. Voyager
(
Wang et al., 2023
)
and ExpeL
(
Zhao et al., 2024
)
learn reusable skills or experience from successful episodes. Among these, Reflexion is the directly comparable baseline in our setting: it requires only a scalar success/failure indicator, applies failure-triggered verbal memory updates, and needs no task-specific engineering to operate with CAGE-2’s per-step reward signal. The remaining methods would each require nontrivial adaptation: Voyager and ExpeL depend on reusable successes, scarce at CAGE-2 initialization where zero-shot performance is near-catastrophic; CLIN is built for structured text-simulator feedback rather than scalar per-step reward; Dynamic Cheatsheet
(
Suzgun et al., 2025
)
and ACE
(
Zhang et al., 2025
)
use update regimes that differ from scalar per-step cyber-defense reward; and TextGrad would require an auxiliary evaluator to convert environment reward into the textual optimization signal it expects (it is the most tractable future comparison). We therefore adopt Reflexion as the primary baseline and compare it against FORGE under identical model, memory representation, and training budget.

evidence.quote:
Champion Broadcast.

After each stage, a frozen checkpoint evaluation produces a return
R
i
R_{i}
for each active instance. The instance with the highest checkpoint return among active (non-graduated) instances is designated the
champion
, and its complete memory state replaces the memory of every other active instance. This is a destructive operation: each recipient discards its own accumulated artifacts and begins the next stage from the champion’s memory. The design prioritizes convergence toward the best-discovered strategy over preserving population diversity.
evidence.support_explanation: A frozen checkpoint selects a single champion whose full memory destructively overwrites other active instances; diversity loss is explicit.

evidence.quote:
Graduation and Early Stopping.

Instances whose checkpoint return exceeds a graduation threshold
θ
\theta
are
graduated
: their memory is frozen and they are excluded from all subsequent stages. Graduation prevents regression by locking strong solutions before the next broadcast cycle can overwrite them, and conserves compute by excluding converged instances from further training.

When broadcast is disabled (condition =
Reflexion
), the protocol reduces to parallel independent Reflexion, the baseline against which FORGE is compared. After all stages complete, every instance (graduated or not) undergoes a final frozen evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: Graduation freezes selected memory, excludes it from later stages, and all instances receive a final frozen evaluation; Reflexion disables broadcast.

evidence.quote:
Population Broadcast vs. Isolated Reflexion.

Comparing FORGE against the Reflexion baseline isolates the contribution of population-level knowledge transfer (Figure
5
, Panel A). FORGE improves post-session evaluation return by 29-72% over Reflexion in all 12 model-representation conditions (Table
3
,
Δ
\Delta
Refl columns). The no-graduation variant also outperforms Reflexion in all 12 conditions, confirming that champion broadcast is the essential mechanism. Reflexion instances exhibit persistently high volatility across stages (Figure
5
, Panel B), whereas FORGE steadily compresses score variance.

5.2.
Ablation: No-Graduation

The no-graduation variant retains champion broadcast but keeps all 10 instances active throughout all 6 stages, isolating the contribution of graduation from that of broadcast. Across models, FORGE reduces the active instance count as stages progress (Figure
6
, Panel A, solid lines), with per-instance adaptation cost dropping as instances graduate. The no-graduation variant (dashed) consumes roughly twice the adaptation tokens per instance by S6 (Figure
6
, Panel B). The effect of graduation on final performance is model-dependent: removing it helps Grok and Qwen (up to 67% improvement over FORGE, Table
3
), while Gemini and Llama perform better with graduation in 2 of 3 representations. This split suggests that graduation’s memory-freezing mechanism protects strong early-stage artifacts in some models but terminates learning prematurely in others. Both FORGE variants outperform the Reflexion baseline in all 12 conditions, confirming that broadcast is the essential mechanism regardless of whether graduation is enabled.
evidence.support_explanation: Broadcast versus Reflexion and no-graduation ablation support a broadcast contribution; freezing can hurt Grok/Qwen and is not uniformly beneficial.

evidence.support_explanation: Per-stage and final tables expose uncertainty and failures. The prose says Grok Rules stages 4-6 are about -224, but Table 19 gives -43.39/-48.49/-51.75. Llama Rules final -81.34 also differs from Table 3 -72.0. These are author-side reporting discrepancies, not absent full text.
Failure-trigger alternatives have only 2-3 sessions and show a nonmonotone threshold response, limiting a universal optimal-trigger claim.

evidence.quote:
FORGE
: Population-based continual learning (champion broadcast)

Reflexion
: Single-instance learning (no population broadcast)

Key Metrics

Evaluation Reward
: Cumulative reward per episode (Higher is better)

Graduation Rate
: % of learning stages successfully completed

Token Efficiency
: Total tokens processed to reach performance

Volatility
: Standard deviation of rewards across stages

Scale

Zero-Shot: 5 experiments, 270 episodes

Reflexion: 38 experiments, 1,000 episodes

FORGE: 49 experiments, 890 episodes

FORGE w/o grad: 24 experiments, 480 episodes

Total
: 116 experiments, 2,640 episodes, 12364.0M tokens
evidence.support_explanation: Table 7 gives 116 experiments, 2640 episodes, 12364M tokens. This reporting basis is not reconciled with main-text/token-per-instance figures.

signatures.object: Role-specific dynamic natural-language memory for Planner/Analyst/ActionChooser
signatures.information: Same frozen LLM, failed trajectory, numeric simulator reward and captured environment state; ActionChooser/learning agents additionally receive action reference; no stronger teacher.
signatures.operation: Abort when step reward < -1.1; Reflector/Exemplifier writes conditional rules or ReAct examples; append and restart, at most 3 attempts/stage.
signatures.conditions: Scalar feedback must diagnose useful failures; context must accommodate memory; negative return is better closer to zero.
signatures.selection_rule: Inner edits are appended, not independently counterfactually admitted; later checkpoints select whole memories.
signatures.persistence: Memory files on disk, injected into every later attempt.
signatures.later_use: Next attempt and later stage; frozen final evaluation.
signatures.claimed_effect: Reduce failure and improve sequential defense decisions.
signatures.failure_boundary: No paired successful-versus-failed contrast required; unsound lessons can accumulate; exact capacity/eviction unspecified.

signatures.information: One frozen checkpoint episode return per active instance, not final post-session report.
signatures.operation: After each stage select argmax checkpoint among nongraduates; replace every active memory with champion; re-explore independently next stage.
signatures.output: Shared elite memory and new descendant variants
signatures.conditions: Checkpoint ranking must transfer to report performance; destructive replacement sacrifices complementary discoveries.
signatures.selection_rule: Single-best nongraduated checkpoint winner; no uncertainty-adjusted comparison or paired incumbent test.
signatures.persistence: Full champion state copied between stages and retained for subsequent episodes.
signatures.later_use: Up to 6 stages then separate learning-disabled evaluation.
signatures.claimed_effect: 29-72% lower negative-return magnitude than isolated Reflexion, across 12 settings.
signatures.failure_boundary: Single noisy probe, diversity collapse, occasional regression; not a statistically sound commit rule.

signatures.operation: Freeze memory and remove instance from subsequent training/broadcast; still evaluate all final instances.
signatures.output: Protected incumbents and reduced active compute
signatures.conditions: Checkpoint must indicate genuinely stable competence.
signatures.selection_data: Same checkpoint source as champion selection
signatures.persistence: Graduates remain frozen through the remainder of session.
signatures.claimed_effect: Compute savings rather than universal return improvement.
signatures.failure_boundary: Early freeze can terminate useful adaptation; no-graduation improves Grok/Qwen.

gap.author_gap: Single-stream prompt reflection lacks robust propagation/selection in stochastic long-horizon POMDPs; memory representations and cross-family effects need controlled comparisons.
gap.checked_gap: A concrete local instability gap is demonstrated against isolated Reflexion; contribution is broadcast/synchronization and freezing, not simply learning without weights. Broad novelty over PBT/prompt evolution is not independently established.

lineage.version: cited in fixed 2605.16233v1, original not supplied
lineage.relation: Failure-triggered verbal-memory ancestor, directly implemented baseline

lineage.source: Population Based Training (Jaderberg et al., 2017) and prompt evolution
lineage.version: cited in fixed 2605.16233v1, originals not supplied
lineage.relation: Exploit/explore transplanted to discrete text; full replacement instead of interpolation

gap.residue: Who should propagate which memory under noisy fitness, without losing good artifacts or spending all instances through all stages?
gap.stakes: Near-catastrophic empty-memory returns and persistent instability in isolated streams.
gap.method_response: Failure-derived artifacts, executable selection, stagewise champion replacement and frozen graduates.
gap.remaining_gap: Independent neighbor verification; stronger alternative inner loops/selectors; attacker/domain transfer; sound noisy-selection gate; accounting/table reconciliation.
unresolved: Original nearest-neighbor full texts absent from fixed package; request shared fixed neighbor packet if comparative novelty must be settled.
Original seed logs/artifact snapshots not provided; no external reproduction claimed.

rs_pattern.reason: Primary: frees the isolated fixed memory-propagation/update regime of a staged generation procedure; supporting: explicitly injects evolved memory into frozen agents. Subcards are not forced by application terminology.

tactic_steps_checked: Names isolated stream as fixed incumbent
matches.reason: Actual iterative memory pipeline is redesigned, not a geometric substrate (C15), diffusion-chain derivation (C23), or iterative generative-backbone interface/latent redesign (C24). Null sub preserves original tactic boundaries.

tactic_steps_checked: Reads it at inference without model updates
failure_checks: No heterogeneous canonical family/substrate or upstream schema-learning stage
matches.reason: Parent conditioning operation is real; C03 full tactic requires broad canonical schema/reference substrate and category-level generalization absent here; local same-environment memory does not instantiate that whole tactic.

condition_checks.reason: Outcome signal is simulator reward, not reflector self-approval.
Fixed capacity asserted; exact eviction/conflict policy not supplied.
Whole-state checkpoint broadcast, not marginal entry admission.
Fixed executable simulator reward, but single-checkpoint rank can be noisy.
Semantic failure trace grounds each text mutation.

unassigned: No evidence_gated_retention match: raw single-episode argmax/absolute threshold does not measure counterfactual utility or support a statistically sound commit.

Population sub H13 considered but not assigned: its score-driven/undirected variation is not the inner failure-trace diagnosis here; H15 would require credited search-guidance memory distinct from the evolved acting memory.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Redesign isolated staged memory adaptation into executable champion selection and inter-stage inheritance.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions: Trustworthy ranking and enough independent exploration; frozen task model.
pattern_mapping.differences: Not classic diffusion/geometry redesign or fitness-only undirected H13 mutation; single-best destructive broadcast.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Failed episodes become persistent conditional text which is reinjected into subsequent frozen-agent contexts.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions: Outcome-grounded useful abstraction and a later read; neither name alone nor plausible text suffices.
pattern_mapping.differences: Same attacker distribution; no cross-category generalization or C03 upstream schema interpreter.

expectations.applies_when: Persistent prompt learning claims to remove a fixed bottleneck.
expectations.reason: Names unstable isolated propagation and representation choices, not only frozen weights.

expectations.applies_when: Reflection claims to extract task-relevant causal guidance.
expectations.reason: Reward grounding is explicit but artifacts arise from failed trajectories, not systematically paired success/failure contrasts.
Simulator reward triggers reflection independently of same-model artifact plausibility.
On-disk bounded memory and replacement are stated; exact capacity, conflict and retirement algorithm are not clear.

expectations.applies_when: Artifacts are published for later reuse.
expectations.reason: Champion/graduate selection gates whole states but append-only inner artifacts have no independent marginal test.
Changes population propagation/synchronization rather than merely changing application.
Executable reward is fixed and targets defense; single probe is a noisy selector and rank transfer is imperfect.
Memory is role-scaffolded but whole-state mutation/overwrite lacks a quantified small-genome capacity.
Reflector sees actual failed trajectories and reward.
No-broadcast/no-graduation arms test whole retained structure, but no entry-level child-parent attribution.

expectations.applies_when: Method enlarges text search into whole configurations or code.
expectations.reason: FORGE retains text artifacts throughout; no enlarged genome claim to justify.

expectations.applies_when: Retained improvement rather than selected checkpoint gain.
expectations.reason: Learning-disabled final reports are separate from checkpoint selection, but exact nonoverlap of seeds is not specified and original seeds are not bundled.

expectations.applies_when: Broadcast is claimed as critical rather than generic selection.
expectations.reason: Same backbone/representation and capped protocol plus no-graduation isolate much of broadcast; no random-champion selector or fully matched-token alternative optimizer.

expectations.applies_when: Stochastic POMDP claims reliability across independent evolutions.
expectations.reason: Repeated sessions and session SD/episode SD exist, but no full hierarchical confidence analysis/significance tests and denominator inconsistencies remain.

expectations.applies_when: Graduation/Rules are claimed to save actual compute.
expectations.reason: Costs of adaptation/evaluation are discussed and no-graduation costs more, but differing total/per-instance bases and missing original logs prevent exact efficiency audit.

claims.text: FORGE improves all 12 model/representation settings over zero-shot and Reflexion.
claims.setting: CAGE-2 B_line, 13-host network, 30 steps; four frozen model families and three representations.
claims.baseline_control: Same hierarchy with empty memory; isolated Reflexion; 10-instance/6-stage/3-attempt protocol caps.
claims.selection_vs_test: Single-episode checkpoints choose champions/graduation; post-session frozen episodes report results; explicit seed lists absent.
claims.result_denominator: Author Table 3: Gemini Examples -24.5 versus zero-shot -189.6 and Reflexion -78.9; 7 primary sessions/representation, 3-4 others; full counts internally inconsistent in appendix.
claims.allowed_conclusion: In-distribution retained-memory effect is supported in direction, but do not treat every tabulated exact mean or pooled denominator as reconciled.

claims.text: Population broadcast is the critical mechanism; graduation mainly saves compute.
claims.setting: Broadcast enabled/disabled; same frozen models, three memory encodings; no-graduation has 2 sessions/condition.
claims.baseline_control: Reflexion without broadcast; FORGE without graduation.
claims.selection_vs_test: Same checkpoint selection design, frozen final evaluation.
claims.result_denominator: Both broadcast variants outperform isolated Reflexion in all 12 tabulated conditions; removing graduation can improve Grok/Qwen up to 67% relative.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Broadcast contributes beyond isolated learning under stated protocol caps; no proof of optimal selector, universal graduation advantage or fully cost-matched superiority.

claims.text: Rules uses roughly 40% fewer tokens with best cost-reliability profile.
claims.baseline_control: Rules versus Examples and Mixed with identical protocol form.
claims.selection_vs_test: Training + final report cost is claimed; memory length/graduation alter executed budget.
claims.result_denominator: Main text ~106M/177M/188M; appendix adaptation averages 7.3M/8.4M/10.2M per instance; Table 7 pooled 12364M.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Compact rules and early freezing have plausible/measured cost benefits, but exact ~40% accounting is not independently reconciled; no deployment-wide efficiency claim.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported frozen post-session episodes support that retained whole memories improve in-distribution B_line/30-step performance relative to empty memory and isolated reflection. Broadcast has an ablation-supported effect; this is neither independent reproduction nor an improved improver, and exact universality/magnitudes and cost advantage need table reconciliation.
unresolved: Selection/report seed disjointness is not explicitly auditable from supplied text.
Table 3/Table 19 and Appendix G.1 contradict some means/SD and prose; precise numbers should not be silently corrected.
Token accounting and the ~40% Rules efficiency claim are not fully reconciled across the main text, Table 7 and per-instance appendix.

G.reason: Specific instability/propagation gap and Reflexion/PBT lineage are identified with a relevant baseline; fixed packet lacks independent originals and stronger inner-loop comparisons.

M.reason: Failure-derived memory plus checkpoint inheritance directly targets unstable isolated streams and yields ablatable predictions. Single-probe ranking and destructive replacement remain heuristic.

X.reason: Proposal, disk write, checkpoint selector, overwrite, freeze and subsequent reads are reconstructable; exact capacity/eviction and reliable rollback/uncertainty gate are incomplete. Raw selection is not evidence-gated counterfactual admission.

E.measurement.reason: Executable simulator returns have a clear direction and frozen report mode; checkpoint maxima are distinguished. Exact reward summaries/SD disagree between tables and tail thresholds vary (<-100 versus <-150), so measurement reporting is not fully auditable.

E.causality.reason: Matched frozen models/representations, no-broadcast and no-graduation arms isolate much of the contribution; no random-selector or alternative inner optimizer control and no exact token-matched comparison prevent a top causal rating.

E.holdout.reason: Final frozen episodes do not write back and are distinguished from selection checkpoints, supporting in-distribution retention rather than checkpoint cherry-picking. Explicit seed disjointness/audit is missing; no cross-attacker transfer is claimed.

E.statistics.reason: Independent evolution sessions, within/across-session SD, SEM, raw failures and counts exist, satisfying repeat/variance evidence beyond a single run. No multi-seed interval/significance suite; pooled and per-arm denominators do not reconcile, limiting exact reliability claims.

E.cost.reason: Adaptation/evaluation and reflection token costs are exposed and graduation cost effects are ablated; main-text totals, appendix per-instance basis and pooled totals need reconciliation, and original logs/seeds are unavailable. This accounting deficiency is assessed here, not again as a causal budget penalty.

rationale: 失败轨迹写入并复用文本记忆，广播消融支持同分布留存收益；单次检查选优不构成统计门控。表格、失败口径与成本账不一致，跨域与替代优化器证据不足，结论限于B_line/30步。
